title: PurchaseOrder
description:
A buyer issued purchase contract, also called a purchase order.
Carries all eleven `credentialSubject` properties of the UNVTD purchase order
(https://unvtd.unece.org/docs/purchase-order/#schema). The seller issued
mirror of this document is {@link ITradeAgreement}.
See docs/model-guide.md §2.4 for the property mapping and its trade-offs.

issueDateTime.description: The date the order was issued. UNVTD `orderDate`.

buyerParty.description: The buyer party placing this order. UNVTD `buyer`.

sellerParty.description: The seller party the order is placed with. UNVTD `seller`.

deliveryLocation.description:
Where the goods are to be delivered. UNVTD `deliveryLocation`.
Other places, such as a place of payment presentation, go in the
inherited `applicableLocation`.

includedSupplyChainTradeLineItem.description: An ordered lot. UNVTD `orderedItems`, minimum one.

applicableDeliveryTerms.description:
The delivery terms in coded form: the Incoterm and its named place. The
verbatim source text of the same row is in `basis`.

purchaseConditionsDocument.description:
A document setting conditions on this order, such as a supplier code of
conduct.

contractDocument.description:
A document whose terms govern this order, such as a standard trade
contract or a supplier code of conduct.

paymentMethod.description: The means by which payment is to be made. UNVTD `paymentMethod`.

allowanceCharge.description: An allowance or charge applied to this order. UNVTD `allowanceCharge`.

totalOrderAmount.description: The total amount of this order. UNVTD `totalOrderAmount`.

invoiceeParty.description: The party to be invoiced, when neither buyer nor seller. UNVTD `invoicee`.

applicableHeaderTradeDelivery.description:
The shipping details: instructions, despatch and delivery events, ship-to
and ship-from parties, consignments, packaging and transport equipment.

includedNote.description:
Contractual prose with no typed UN/CEFACT slot, discriminated by
`subject`. The insurance allocation lives here: UN/CEFACT has no
insurance property on any header class.

Date.title: Date
Date.description:
A date carried by a trade document.
`DateValue` is an unconstrained string for now, so it accepts the document's
own wording as well as a normalised form. No `format` is asserted until the
representation is settled.

DateValue.description: The date, as printed on the document or normalised.

TradeParty.title: TradeParty
TradeParty.description:
A party taking a role in a trade document, such as the buyer or the seller.
Only the name is mandatory: sample documents identify counterparties by name
alone, so requiring an address would reject a real document. The address,
role codes, identifiers and contacts are all inherited and optional.

name.description: A name, expressed as text, for this trade party.

brandName.description: A brand name, expressed as text, for this trade party.

emailURICommunication.description: The email communication for this trade party.

postalAddress.description: The postal address for this trade party.

telephoneCommunication.description: A telephone communication for this trade party.

Location.title: Location
Location.description:
A place named by a trade document, such as a destination or a place of
payment presentation. Use `locationFunctionTypeCode` to say which.

name.description: A name, expressed as text, of this logistics related location.

postalAddress.description: The postal trade address information for this logistics related location.

Basis.title: Basis
Basis.description:
The trading basis of a document, verbatim as printed on its `Basis` row: the
delivery term, the weight basis, any franchise and the tare method.

The coded Incoterm and its named place are carried separately in
`applicableDeliveryTerms`; this is the verbatim source text.

BasisValue.description:
The verbatim text of the `Basis` row, for example
`FOB origin, N.S.W, 0.5% franchise, Actual Tare.`

Insurance.title: Insurance
Insurance.description:
How insurance is allocated between the parties, verbatim as printed on the
`Insurance` row.

UN/CEFACT has no insurance property on any header class —
`IUneceCargoInsurance` hangs off a physical consignment — so there is no
structured alternative to grow into yet.

InsuranceValue.description:
The verbatim text of the `Insurance` row, for example
`For buyer's account.`

PaymentTerms.title: PaymentTerms
PaymentTerms.description:
The terms of payment agreed for a trade document. Carry the verbatim text in
`description` and the code list value in `paymentTermsTypeCode`.

information.description: Information, expressed as text, for these trade payment terms.

billStartDateTime.description: The date, time, date time, or other date time value of the bill start specified by these trade payment terms.

dueDateTime.description: The date, time, date time, or other date time value of the due date specified by these trade payment terms.

Conditions.title: Conditions
Conditions.description:
Conditions the document is subject to, verbatim as printed on its
`Conditions` row.

Referenced governing documents stay in `contractDocument` and
`purchaseConditionsDocument`.

ConditionsValue.description:
The verbatim text of the `Conditions` row, for example
`Subject to approval of preshipment sample by buyer.`

DeliveryTerms.title: DeliveryTerms
DeliveryTerms.description:
The delivery terms of a trade document. The Incoterm goes in
`deliveryTermsDeliveryTypeCode` and its named place in `relevantLocation`;
weight basis, tolerance and tare rules have no typed slot and go verbatim in
`description`.

PaymentMeans.title: PaymentMeans
PaymentMeans.description:
The means by which a payment is to be made, such as a transfer, a cheque or
a documentary credit.

AllowanceCharge.title: AllowanceCharge
AllowanceCharge.description:
An allowance or a charge applied to a trade document. `chargeIndicator` is
mandatory because it is what distinguishes the two.

chargeIndicator.description: The indication of whether or not the trade allowance charge is a charge.

Amount.title: Amount
Amount.description:
A monetary amount. Both the value and its currency are mandatory: an amount
without one of them cannot be acted on.
